source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 2 (questions: PDF pages 14–17, answers: PDF pages 111–112)

questions.rule: The arms of the cross appear and then become double, one direction at a time.
questions.working: Figure 1: single up-and-down lines. Figure 2: single side lines are added. Figure 3: the up-and-down lines become double. So in figure 4 the side lines become double too: option A.

questions.rule: The shaded part of the ring moves bottom, top, right, left, and the centre is white and shaded in turn.
questions.working: Figure 4 comes after the right side, so the ring is shaded on the left. The centre is white in figures 1 and 3 and shaded in figure 2, so it is shaded in figure 4: option D.

questions.rule: The lines turn 45° anticlockwise each time, carrying the shapes with them, and black and white swap each time.
questions.working: Turn figure 3 by 45° anticlockwise: the triangle goes to the left, the black circle to the lower right and the white circle to the top. Then swap black and white: a white triangle on the left, a white circle lower down and a black circle at the top: option C.

questions.rule: The shaded quarter moves one quarter clockwise each time.
questions.working: Top-left, top-right, bottom-right, so next the bottom-left quarter is shaded, with the same lines across. Options B and C both have that; the book says the small circles change between one and two, and C has one white circle: option C.
questions.note: All three figures in the question show two small circles, so the circles alone don't show the pattern the book describes. The choice between B (a black dot) and C (a white circle) rests on the book's explanation.

questions.rule: The four parts are mirror images: each has a line from its outer corner to the centre, with a small circle at that corner.
questions.working: The top-left part has its circle at the top-left corner, the top-right part at the top-right corner, and the bottom-left part at the bottom-left corner. So the bottom-right part has a line from the bottom-right corner with the circle there: option D.

questions.rule: The outside shape gets one more side each time, and the inside shape one less.
questions.working: Outside: triangle (3), rectangle (4), pentagon (5), so next a hexagon (6). Inside: square (4 lines), triangle (3), two lines (2), so next a single line (1): option D.

questions.rule: One more curved arrow each time, and the arrows go anticlockwise and clockwise in turn.
questions.working: 1 arrow going anticlockwise, 2 going clockwise, 3 going anticlockwise, so next 4 arrows all going clockwise. Only in C do all four arrows go clockwise: option C.

questions.rule: Each figure is a path of straight lines with right-angle turns, one line longer than the one before.
questions.working: 2 lines, 3 lines, 4 lines, so next a path of 5 lines.
questions.note: Hidden: options C and D are the same shape (D is only drawn in a taller box), so the key's D is not the only right option.

questions.rule: The small ovals swap sides of the line each time, and one more is added every second figure.
questions.working: 1 on the left, 2 on the right, 2 on the left, 3 on the right, 3 on the left, so next 4 on the right: option C.

questions.rule: In figures 1 and 3 the outside shapes are ⊂; in figures 2 and 4 every shape copies the middle shape of the figure before.
questions.working: Figure 1's middle shape is ∩, so figure 2 is ∩∩∩. Figure 3's middle shape is ∪, so figure 4 is ∪∪∪: option D.

questions.rule: One more line each time; the circles go 4, 3, 3.
questions.working: The lines go 1, 2, 3, so the answer has 4 lines.
questions.note: Hidden: the circles go 4, 3, 3. If they should fall to 1, the answer is A (the book's key); if they should stay at 3, it is C. The question can't be settled.

questions.rule: Each time every arrow turns round, the plain line becomes a left arrow, and a new plain line is added at the bottom.
questions.working: Figure 4 is ←, →, ←, then a plain line. Turn each arrow round (→, ←, →), make the line a left arrow (←) and add a line: →, ←, →, ←, line: option B.

questions.rule: The letters go on in order, three at a time. In figures 1, 3 and 5 they are written top, bottom-left, bottom-right; in figures 2 and 4 bottom-right, bottom-left, top.
questions.working: After A–C, D–F, G–I and J–L come M, N, O. Figure 5 is written like figures 1 and 3: M at the top, N bottom-left, O bottom-right: option B.

questions.rule: The chain of circles lies down and stands up in turn, and gets one circle longer every second figure.
questions.working: 3 lying, 3 standing, 4 lying, 4 standing, so next 5 circles lying down: option D.

questions.rule: The curved line goes round the oval (right, below, left, above), facing away from it and towards it in turn.
questions.working: After 'above' the curve comes back to the right side. It faces away in figures 1 and 3, so in figure 5 it faces away too: '(' on the right, as in figure 1: option B.
